Chart type and plotter reference

rvis authors

Source: vignettes/chart-types.Rmd
chart-types.Rmd

This reference documents the chart methods callable through rvisPlot(type, plotter, ...). Dispatch uses the exact function name plotter.type; spelling and capitalization matter. The method inventory below is parsed from the wrapper source rather than inferred from the older compatibility matrix.

Each table gives the exact wrapper function and its formal arguments. Dimension values usually refer to columns in obj, while graph and table methods can accept specialized objects. config is a named list of wrapper-specific settings; the configuration reference lists all keys currently recorded by the package.

Rendered examples of every chart type and plotter are in the topic guides, each built on its own dataset. Each section below links to the examples of its chart type.

Guide Chart types Data
Comparing categories bar, line, area, area range, combo VADeaths
Parts of a whole pie, funnel, pyramid, gauge, bullet, word cloud HairEyeColor
Relationships and distributions scatter, bubble, histogram, box iris
Time series time series line, area and bar, stock, calendar airquality
Networks and hierarchies graph, sankey, sunburst, tree, treemap Titanic
Tables interactive, filterable and pivot tables USArrests

Packages that are not wrapped yet, and how to add a plotter, are in Adding plotters.

Common argument conventions

Argument Common meaning
obj Input data frame or object accepted by the wrapper.
x, y, y2, z Axis or numeric dimensions.
label, theta, group, color, shape, size Category, measure, grouping, and visual mappings.
low, high Range bounds or interval endpoints.
source, target, linkWidth, key Network links and identifiers.
config Named list of settings supported by the selected wrapper.
... Additional arguments forwarded by wrappers that support forwarding.

Legacy chart aliases without dispatch methods

The previous compatibility matrix lists combo.molten, heatmap, and map. The current wrapper source does not define dimple.combo.molten or highcharts.heatmap, and Leaflet’s function is named leaflet.map.plot. Since rvisPlot() dispatches by exact function name, the first two pairs are not callable through rvisPlot() as currently implemented; use type = "map.plot" for the existing Leaflet wrapper.

The exported valid.plot.types vector also contains calheat and motion, but no wrapper methods with those suffixes are currently defined. The calendar wrapper is dispatched with type = "calendar".

calheat

No plotter.calheat wrapper is currently defined. Use the calendar chart method for the calheatmap wrapper.

motion

No wrapper method with the motion suffix is currently defined.

combo.molten

There is no current function named dimple.combo.molten. Use a non-molten combo method that appears in the chart table, or reshape the data to the input format supported by that method.

heatmap

There is no current function named highcharts.heatmap. The capability table lists this pairing, but rvisPlot(type = "heatmap", plotter = "highcharts") cannot dispatch to a wrapper today.

map

The capability table calls the Leaflet method map, while the function is leaflet.map.plot. Use the exact wrapper dispatch shown in the map.plot section.

box charts

Call rvisPlot(type = "box", plotter = "<wrapper>", ...) to select this chart method.

Wrapper methods

plotter value Function Formal arguments
amCharts amCharts.box obj, x = NULL, y = NULL, config = NULL, ...
plotly plotly.box obj, x = NULL, y = NULL, group = NULL, config = NULL, ...
bpexploder bpexploder.box obj, y = NULL, group = NULL, config = NULL, ...

The current bpexploder.box() implementation declares group but refers to an undefined x while preparing its data. That method may fail unless an unrelated x object exists in the calling environment. Use amCharts.box() or plotly.box() for this example until the wrapper is repaired.

graphChart charts

visNetwork.graphChart() is currently an exported placeholder: its body returns an undefined object (v). rvisPlot() can resolve the function name, but it does not currently produce a chart.

map.plot charts

The Leaflet function is named leaflet.map.plot, so it dispatches as type = "map.plot". The legacy compatibility matrix labels it map, but rvisPlot(type = "map", plotter = "leaflet") does not match the current function name.

Wrapper methods

plotter value Function Formal arguments
leaflet leaflet.map.plot x, stores = rownames(sg$spec), tiles = F, icon = NULL

Input requirement

This function only handles objects inheriting from STORE.GROUP; it reads store specifications through a global sg object and does not accept an ordinary data frame. There is no self-contained synthetic example for this legacy wrapper. Its current implementation should be repaired before it is used as a general rvisPlot() map example.

Arguments

Common meanings for the arguments on these methods:

Argument Meaning
x Horizontal axis, time, or primary input; interpretation is wrapper-specific.
stores Store identifiers selected from a STORE.GROUP object.
tiles Whether to add a map tile layer.
icon Leaflet marker icon definition.

Dispatch caveats

rvisPlot() constructs and evaluates the wrapper function name; it does not use data/plotters.csv to validate the selection. The CSV includes historical aliases, so the exact names listed above are authoritative for dispatch. Wrapper methods can also differ in required input shape even when they share a chart type.
